key_check.blind_answer: Two reduced bile-salt functions: (1) emulsification of dietary fat droplets, which increases surface area so pancreatic lipase can digest triglycerides efficiently; (2) micelle formation, which solubilizes and carries lipid digestion products (fatty acids, monoacylglycerides) to the enterocyte brush border for absorption.
key_check.evidence: Re-review, Devin session 59eb4828. Record answer.text ('emulsification of triglycerides, which speeds their digestion by pancreatic lipase, and micelle formation, which carries lipid digestion products to the absorptive epithelial surface') matches the blind answer exactly. It is the unique correct pair as worded: sec23.7 assigns bile salts precisely two roles in lipid handling - 'Bile salts not only speed up lipid digestion' (via the emulsified-triglyceride substrate listed for pancreatic lipase in Table 23.8) 'they are also essential to the absorption of the end products of lipid digestion' (via micelles, without which lipids 'never come in contact with the absorptive surfaces of the epithelial cells').

rationale_check.evidence: Re-review, Devin session 59eb4828. reasoning_chain supports the answer and is internally correct. Step 1 ('Bile salts emulsify dietary triglycerides, and pancreatic lipase acts on these emulsified triglycerides, so bile salts speed up lipid digestion') matches Table 23.8 ('Triglycerides that have been emulsified by bile salts' as pancreatic lipase substrate) and 'Bile salts not only speed up lipid digestion'. Step 2 ('they form micelles that carry the end products of lipid digestion to the intestinal absorptive surface') matches 'bile salts and lecithin resolve this issue by enclosing them in a micelle' and 'essential to the absorption of the end products of lipid digestion'. Step 3 correctly reasons from the stipulations (intact pancreatic enzymes, reduced bile salts) that both the emulsification and micellar delivery steps are impaired and that neither function alone explains the added stool fat - sound internal logic over exempt stipulations. teaching_points entry ('emulsification before lipase acts and micelle formation afterward; bile salts are not themselves pancreatic lipase') is correct: sec23.7 treats emulsification by bile salts and the pancreatic acinar-cell enzyme lipase as distinct entities.

distractor_check.evidence: Re-review, Devin session 59eb4828. Case vignette has no options. Competing interpretations are addressed: the question wording fixes the canonical two bile-salt functions (sec23.7 names exactly two roles - speeding lipid digestion and enabling absorption of its end products), and reasoning_chain step 3 explicitly states neither function alone explains the added stool fat, foreclosing a single-function reading. No unaddressed competing factual claim found.
